First thing on July 4th, Stephanie Edwards stops you in the street about what happened yesterday.
Stephanie Edwards stands at the edge of the room, holding a folded flyer from your campaign. // Stephanie Edwards: I gave what I could. I'd like a minute, if you have one.
Put me down to speak at the next public meeting. I want you to know why. [Replies: I'll read what you send. Put your name on it so I can write back. | My scheduler will find you a slot. Give her your number. | I'll hear you out. I can't promise a vote because of a donation, any size. | Not today. Catch me after the session.] // Stephanie Edwards: MIRA PARSONS
I'll read what you send. Put your name on it so I can write back.
Thank you. I'll be there early.

06.words:
First thing on June 6th, Julia Lambert catches you at school about what happened yesterday.
It's the last day of the school year. Julia Lambert has been meaning to say something. // Julia Lambert: Last day. Can you believe it?
Do you know what you're doing next? [Replies: Something worth doing. I'll know it when I find it. | What are you doing? You go first. | When I know, you'll know. | Ask me again in a month.] // Julia Lambert: MIRA PARSONS
Something worth doing. I'll know it when I find it.
That sounds like you. What made you decide? [Replies: Something worth doing. I'll know it when I see it. | I'll let you know once I figure it out. | Check back in a month. | I have to run. I wish you the best.] // Julia Lambert: MIRA PARSONS
Something worth doing. I'll know it when I see it.
Here? Really? What would you even do? [Replies: Something that matters. I'll know it when I see it. | I'll tell you when I figure it out. | Ask me in a month. | I have to go. Good luck, really.] // Julia Lambert: MIRA PARSONS
Something that matters. I'll know it when I see it.
Good. You'll be good at it.

07.words:
First thing on January 29th, you stay in, still thinking about what happened yesterday.
Joseph Parsons can't let go of a lawyer for tenants facing eviction, and the story in Almont Press is the reason. // Joseph Parsons: What do you make of Almont Press on a lawyer for tenants facing eviction? I can't tell if it's fair. [Replies: Yeah. I've been thinking the same thing for a while. | I read it. I think they've got it backwards. | Which part got to you? | I haven't read it. Don't spoil it for me.] // Joseph Parsons: MIRA PARSONS
Yeah. I've been thinking the same thing for a while.
So why isn't anyone doing anything about a lawyer for tenants facing eviction? We're the ones who live with it. [Replies: Yeah. I think it does matter. I just didn't want to say so. | I saw it. They only told one side of a lawyer for tenants facing eviction, and that's the side people will remember. | I'm sorry. I can't get into this right now.] // Joseph Parsons: MIRA PARSONS
Yeah. I think it does matter. I just didn't want to say so.
Does that mean you'd say something, if someone asked? [Replies: All right, you're right. It bothers me too. | We can both read it and not agree. | Let me read it again before I say anything else.] // Joseph Parsons: MIRA PARSONS
All right, you're right. It bothers me too.
Then what do we do about it? [Replies: I read it twice. I still don't buy it. | I'll think about it. I have to go.] // Joseph Parsons: MIRA PARSONS
I read it twice. I still don't buy it.
That's not how I read it. Where did they go wrong?
I'm going to keep bringing it up.

08.words:
Sofia Pierce: First thing on May 29th, you head to the City Clerk's office to ask about running. Sofia Pierce comes over to the counter. // Sofia Pierce: What can I do for you? [Replies: I want to run for Council member. November 4, 2025 · Held by Stephanie Gordon | I want to run for Mayor. November 4, 2025 · Held by Emma Sellers] // Sofia Pierce: MIRA PARSONS
I want to run for Council member.
So you're running for Council member. You'd serve 4 years. There's no primary for this one, so it all comes down to November 4. You'd have a seat on the Almont Village Council, voting on the budget and every ordinance that comes before it. You've got until July 22 to get it all back to me. [Replies: Alright. I'll take the papers and get started.] // MIRA PARSONS
Alright. I'll take the papers and get started.
